newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Don't feel sorry for Gorbachev - Yeltsin spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Don't feel sorry for Gorbachev - Yeltsin spokesman.

text.p: Former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev is far from poor, the Kremlin said on Friday, brushing aside the ex-leaders complaints about his financial situation.

Gorbachev, 65, lives in a government dacha near Moscow, is provided with a car and three bodyguards, uses the elite Kremlin hospital and has a state pension equivalent to $535 a month -- far more than the average monthly salary -- Sergei Yastrzhembsky, President Boris Yeltsin's spokesman, said.

"At the present time, Gorbachev's pension is about three million rubles," Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing in response to a question on the subject. "Of course, we don't have data on those honoraria the former president receives for his books, appearances, articles and so on."
"On the basis of these figures, I think anyone could make their own conclusions," Yastrzhembsky said in summing up the ex-Soviet president's government pension package.
As he has toured the world in recent months to promote his lengthy memoirs, Gorbachev has often complained about his material well-being in post-perestroika Russia.

"Two dollars! Two dollars! That was my pension! Gorbachev, the former head of state on two dollars!" he told Britain's Guardian newspaper in November, referring to his monthly pension prior to a substantial increase in 1994.
